subject: Request: subprocessor roster and residency evidence for BankCorp pilot
messages:
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bankcorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: procurement@bankcorp.com
Date: 2027-09-18T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessors + cross-border proof for pilot

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for agreeing to run the pilot next month. Procurement needs a compact list of all subprocessors that will process BankCorp data for the pilot, plus a short statement on where data will transit (countries/regions) and any KMS/HSM providers in the chain. We have an internal audit window the week after kickoff and they require:

- Named subprocessors and roles (processing, telemetry, observability)
- Primary egress/ingress countries and any temporary cloud partners
- Evidence of KMS/HSM use and whether keys are customer-managed
- Any subcontractors that might handle logs/metrics

Can you send a single package (spreadsheet + attestations) we can attach to our SOC2 review? If you have a short timeline for when you can provide this, that would be great — our procurement deadline is 2027-09-24.

Best,
Elaine Turner
Vendor Risk Manager
BankCorp Financial

--
Attachment: N/A (they requested evidence in follow-up)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@bankcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-09-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessors + cross-border proof for pilot

Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Attached is a compact roster (subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx) which calls out roles and primary country of processing. High level answers:

- Named subprocessors: See sheet "Roster" — includes telemetry, metrics, caching, KMS, CDN partners.
- Transit/residency: Primary processing will be in us-west1 for the pilot; some metrics and CDN edges may transit via eu-west1 and us-east1. We flag any transient partners in the roster.
- KMS/HSM: We use a customer-managed KMS option for Dedicated/Private customers; for Hosted we use Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed providers. The attached kms_attestation.pdf summarizes key-holding and encryption scope.
- Logs/metrics subcontractors: Observability vendor listed; we only push aggregated telemetry, no raw request content.

We expect this package to be sufficient for procurement's SOC2 evidence intake, but happy to iterate. If procurement needs a formal attestation letter on company letterhead, we can generate one next week.

Deliverables attached: subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx, kms_attestation.pdf, dataflow-egress-diagram.png

Timeline: initial package attached now; can provide a signed attestation by 2027-09-21 if required.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), kms_attestation.pdf (pdf), dataflow-egress-diagram.png (image)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2027-09-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessors + cross-border proof for pilot

Hi Elaine, Karthik —

Adding a couple of clarifications from the runtime/ops side:

- Caching/edge: The CDN partner caches small prefixed artifacts (models' static files) only; request payloads are not cached. We've added explicit TTLs in the roster for anything edge-cached.
- Temporary partners: For the pilot we will not use any 3rd-party temporary enclaves beyond the ones listed; any emergency ops access would be via pre-authorized seats (and logged).
- Data minimization: We will redact any PII before sending usage telemetry to observability vendor. The roster column "PII exposure" flags this per-subprocessor.

If it helps procurement, I attached a compact egress diagram (dataflow-egress-diagram.png) showing which services see decrypted material.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
